FORMAL CASE NO. EA2012-02, IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF 
PUBLIC POWER, LLC, TO SURRENDER ITS ELECTRICITY SUPPLIER LICENSE IN 
THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA, Order No. 23137 

I. 
INTRODUCTION 
1. 
By this Order,1 the Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia 
(“Commission”) grants the request of Public Power, LLC (“Public Power” or “Applicant”) to 
surrender its electricity supplier license. Cancellation of the Applicant’s electricity supplier license 
is effective upon the issuance of this Order. 

II. 
BACKGROUND 
2. 
On March 6, 2012, the Commission granted Public Power a license to operate as 
an electricity supplier in the District of Columbia (“District”) in Order No. 16726.2 On June 5, 
2026, Public Power filed an Application with the Commission to surrender its electricity supplier 
license.3 Public Power was approved to operate as a marketer of electricity services, but it conducts 
no business and has no customers in the District.4 Consequently, Public Power requests to 
surrender its electricity supplier license.5 

1 
This Order is issued under delegated authority pursuant to Order No. 21981. See Formal Case No. 712, In 
the Matter of the Investigation into the Public Service Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, Order 
No. 21981, ¶ 2. (m), issued April 24, 2024 (“The Commission’s General Counsel, or his or her designee, is delegated 
authority to act and issue orders on the following matters: . . . m. Applications for the Abandonment of Gas or Electric 
Licenses”). Any party may file a petition for reconsideration of the General Counsel’s decision with the Commission. 
2

Supplier License (“Formal Case No. EA2012-02”), Order No. 16726, rel. March 6, 2012.

III. 
DISCUSSION 

3. 
According to 15 DCMR § 4602.10 (a)(1), a licensed electricity supplier wishing to 
cease providing services in the District is required to provide written notice to the Commission of 
the licensee’s intention to cease providing electricity service to its customers and inform its 
customers of the choice to revert to the default service provider or another electricity supplier. 
Section 4602.10 (a)(2) also requires that the surrendering licensee provide to the Commission an 
example or copy of the notice it provided to its customers and, upon the Commission’s receipt of 
such notice, may order the licensee to provide such further notice to its customers or the public as 
the Commission deems necessary, and/or take such other action that the Commission considers 
appropriate.6 

4. 
In the instant case, Public Power’s Application provides the required notice to the 
Commission of its intention to surrender its electricity supplier license.7 Public Power also states 
that the notice requirement to customers is not applicable because it has no customers in the District 
that would require notification.8 Accordingly, Public Power’s Application satisfies the notice 
requirement with regard to the cessation of service. 

5. 
In all other respects, Public Power’s Application conforms with Commission 
requirements for a surrendering licensee. Commission records confirm the Applicant’s submission 
of the case number, order number, and date the Applicant’s license was granted.9 Public Power 
avers, and Commission records confirm that the Applicant’s most recent survey response indicates 
no jurisdictional revenue and that it owes no outstanding debt or fees.10 In addition, the Applicant 
states that it has no outstanding consumer complaints.11 Lastly, the Applicant has submitted an 
affidavit from an officer of Public Power attesting to the truth and accuracy of the information 
submitted.12 

6. 
Based upon the preceding information, the Commission grants Public Power’s 
request to surrender its electricity supplier license granted by Order No. 16726. Cancellation of 
Public Power’s electricity supplier license shall become effective upon the issuance of this Order. 
Should Public Power seek to re-enter the District’s electricity market in the future, it shall have to 
reapply for an electricity supplier license pursuant to Chapter 46 of the Commission’s rules.
